name: kickoff
description: Kick off a new project with one standard questionnaire that collects what is known and makes the starting decisions with you. It is generic: it names no language, stack, vendor or tool — those come from the answers, and Claude proposes the options that depend on them. Questions branch on earlier answers and are asked in dependency order, each with pre-defined options (at most four) and a default; questions about the sibling plugins (crew, task, task-roadmap) are asked only when they are installed. A quality level (None, Basic, Standard, Full) decides the generic checks per aspect, and each aspect then asks only what to drop or add. Answers are recorded in the project; a charter (overview, goal, scope, numbered decisions with their reasons, open questions) and a quality doc are generated from them. Questions with a real trade-off — the quality level, when backward compatibility starts to apply — are always asked explicitly. It then sets the project up: a small instructions-only CLAUDE.md, and the task config with a workflow carrying the practices you keep (INVEST, tests first, SOLID, DRY), in the repo or outside it for a client project. A machine-wide dev-port registry hands each project a free port, and your own defaults, kept per Claude account, override the questionnaire's. On an existing project it proposes answers from what the project already holds — its files, README, docs and code — each with evidence, marks them recovered in the charter, then closes the gaps between the answers and the code (each one done now, made a task, or left by your choice); edited files are shown as a diff instead of overwritten. When the project has browser E2E tests it asks whether to add an optional E2E viewer — every test's last result in the browser, a step-by-step replay of a kept trace, run-and-watch any one test, local only — and hands over the spec for it: the behaviour, the security rules, acceptance scenarios, the recommended tool and the pitfalls already hit; the project builds it. Runtime-free (bash + awk).
